key_insight: Sr2+ doping in Nd2-xSrxCoMnO6-δ drives a structural and magnetic transition that can switch exchange bias from normal to robust inverse behavior, with the strongest effect near x = 0.75.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that cation substitution can be used to tune interfacial magnetic states in double perovskites, which is relevant for designing low-temperature spintronic and magnetic memory materials.
method: Neutron powder diffraction to track the monoclinic-to-rhombohedral structural evolution and B-site disorder
X-ray absorption spectroscopy to estimate Co/Mn valence changes with Sr doping
DC magnetization and AC susceptibility to probe ferromagnetism, cluster-glass behavior, and exchange bias
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a maximum exchange-bias field of about 4 kOe at 8 K under a 6 T cooling field, with robust inverse exchange bias persisting after minor-loop correction.
watch_item: The exchange-bias behavior is strongly temperature- and field-dependent, so minor-loop effects and cooling-field conditions must be carefully controlled when comparing samples.
paper_title: Antisite-disorder driven tuning of magnetic properties and exchange-bias in Nd$_{2-x}$Sr$_{x}$CoMnO$_{6-δ}$ $(0 \leq x \leq 1)$ ($δ\sim 0.5$) double perovskites
